Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions are to register for questions using the one-by-one method. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are David Harper, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; Raj Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; and Emily Santos, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to a variety of factors. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Harper.

David Harper:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives across AI-enhanced project management and workflow automation.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: strengthening our LTV/CAC ratio, providing solid ARR guidance for the next quarter, conducting thorough churn analysis with effective mitigation strategies, maintaining a robust cash position and runway, driving expansion revenue from existing customers, and upholding our strong Rule of 40 metric.

These efforts reflect the scalability of our SaaS model and our ability to deliver value in a competitive landscape. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $178 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $28 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $700 million to $720 million in ARR exiting the fiscal year.

Let me elaborate further on the six key areas David highlighted, as they underscore the health of our business. Starting with our key unit economics, which continue to highlight the scalability and efficiency of our SaaS model here at CloudForge. I'm pleased to report that our Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio, or LTV/CAC, came in at 4.2x for Q3, marking a sequential improvement from 4.0x in Q2 and a robust year-over-year gain from 3.5x in Q3 of last year. For context, this significantly outperforms the SaaS industry benchmark of around 3x, as tracked by indices like Benchmarkit and SaaS Capital, and positions us favorably against peers like Asana and Monday.com, who have hovered in the 3.2x to 3.8x range in their recent filings.

To give you a deeper view, our LTV calculation is based on a cohort-forward model using the past 12 months of data, projecting gross profit over the average customer lifetime—factoring in our average ARR per user of $18K for SMBs, $75K for mid-market, and $250K+ for enterprises—discounted at a conservative 10% rate and adjusted for our industry-leading 118% Net Revenue Retention or NRR. Meanwhile, CAC is our fully loaded Weighted Average CAC, including sales commissions, marketing spend, content, and sales engineer time, divided by new logos added in the cohort.

Here's the segment breakdown: In SMB/Self-Serve, which represents 42% of ARR, LTV/CAC is at 4.5x, up from 4.1x YoY. LTV here is $12,400, driven by our product-led growth or PLG motion, where customers self-onboard via our freemium tier and convert at 28% within 90 days—similar to how Notion scaled its viral loops. CAC has dropped 15% QoQ to $2,800, thanks to optimized Google Ads bidding with our in-house ML algorithms and SEO content scaling to 2M monthly visitors.

For Mid-Market, 35% of ARR, it's steady at 4.1x, with LTV of $85K. This segment benefits from our ForgeAI upsell engine, which uses predictive analytics to recommend premium modules like AI-driven resource allocation—boosting expansion ARR by 22% per account.

Enterprise, 23% of ARR, is our star performer at 4.3x, improved from 3.9x last quarter. LTV exceeds $320K, fueled by multi-year contracts averaging 4.2 years, while CAC held flat at $74K despite longer sales cycles averaging 7 months. Key wins include Fortune 500 deals with integrations to Salesforce and Workday.

Regionally, performance is strong but differentiated: North America, 72% of ARR, at 4.5x LTV/CAC, our core market where PLG and field sales synergy shines. EMEA, 18% of ARR, at 3.9x, up 20% YoY as we ramp localized go-to-market with GDPR-compliant AI features and partnerships like our new reseller agreement with Crayon Group, mirroring HubSpot's EMEA playbook. APAC, 10% of ARR, at 3.2x, still maturing but accelerating with 35% QoQ new logo growth. CAC here is higher at $45K due to channel investments, but early LTV signals from Japan and Australia cohorts show 125% NRR, positioning us to hit 4x by year-end as we launch Mandarin support in Q4.

What's driving this trend? First, CAC efficiency gains: We've reduced blended CAC by 12% YoY through technical initiatives like our AI-powered lead scoring in Salesforce Einstein, which improved conversion rates by 18%, and a shift to 55% PLG-driven acquisitions—reducing reliance on high-touch sales from 65% two years ago. Content syndication via LinkedIn and programmatic ads now yields $4.50 revenue per dollar spent, up from $3.20.

On the LTV side, churn compression is key: Gross dollar retention hit 92%, down from 88% last year, thanks to ForgeAI's churn prediction model—achieving 85% accuracy in flagging at-risk accounts and automating personalized retention plays, like dynamic pricing nudges. We've also seen 25% expansion in seat velocity via seamless Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations, tapping into the collaboration software tailwind amid hybrid work persistence.

Strategically, this 4.2x ratio gives us ample Rule of 40 headroom—our growth is 32% YoY while free cash flow margins expand to 28%—allowing us to invest aggressively in R&D for ForgeAI 2.0, which we previewed last quarter. Looking forward, we're targeting 4.5x+ by fiscal 2025 through three levers: doubling PLG down-funnel conversion with in-app AI trials, enterprise land-and-expand via industry vertical packs like fintech and healthcare akin to ServiceNow's approach, and geographic acceleration with $50M allocated to APAC/EMEA channel partners.

In short, our LTV/CAC trajectory validates the durability of our AI-differentiated moat in the $100B+ project management SaaS market, even amidst macro headwinds like elongated sales cycles.

Building on that efficiency, let's turn to expansion revenue from existing customers, one of our most critical growth drivers and the hallmark of our land-and-expand strategy for the CloudForge platform—a comprehensive AI-enhanced collaboration suite that powers workflows for over 15,000 enterprise customers worldwide. In Q3, expansion revenue reached $38.2 million, marking a robust 42% year-over-year increase from $26.9 million in Q3 last year. This not only outpaced our overall revenue growth of 32% but also represented 25% of our total quarterly revenue of $178 million. For context, our dollar-based net retention rate—or DNR—stood at 128%, meaning our existing customer base, defined as those with at least 12 months of tenure, expanded their annual contract value by an average of 28% over the prior year. This is up from 122% in Q3 last year and continues to trend above our long-term target of 120-125%, putting us in elite company alongside leaders like Snowflake and ServiceNow.

Breaking it down by source, upsell revenue accounted for $24.7 million, or 65% of expansion, driven primarily by customers upgrading to our premium tiers—Enterprise Plus and our new AI Pro suite. We've seen particularly strong uptake here, with ACV expansion averaging 18% per upsell customer, fueled by modular add-ons like our ForgeAI Analytics engine, which delivers predictive workflow optimization and real-time collaboration insights. For example, a Fortune 500 financial services client expanded their deployment from 5,000 to 12,000 seats in Q3, adding $1.2 million in incremental ACV by layering on AI-driven sentiment analysis for customer support tickets.

Cross-sell revenue contributed $9.8 million, or 26% of expansion, up 55% YoY, as customers adopted adjacent modules within our ecosystem. Our integrations with key enterprise stacks—Salesforce CRM, SAP S/4HANA, and Workday—have been game-changers, enabling seamless data flows that unlock new use cases. Take our recent launch of ForgeSecure, our zero-trust security module: it drove $4.5 million in cross-sells alone, with adoption rates hitting 32% among mid-market customers, those with $100K-$1M ACV. This mirrors the playbook we've seen from Okta, where security bolt-ons have supercharged expansion in a post-ransomware world.

The remaining $3.7 million, or 9%, came from consumption-based usage spikes, a tailwind unique to our usage-tiered pricing model, akin to Datadog's metrics ingestion. With macroeconomic uncertainty lingering, our customers are optimizing rather than expanding headcount, leading to 15% higher usage in high-velocity modules like our API calls for custom automations.

Regionally, North America remains our expansion powerhouse, delivering $25.4 million, or 66% of total expansion, with a DNR of 132%, bolstered by deep penetration in tech hubs like Silicon Valley and NYC. Our customer success teams have been instrumental, achieving a Net Promoter Score of 68 and reducing churn to under 4% TCV-weighted. In EMEA, expansion hit $7.9 million, up 21% from Q2, as GDPR-compliant AI features resonated with enterprises in the DAX 40; DNR here improved to 124% amid easing inflation in the Eurozone. APAC contributed $4.9 million, with 29% YoY growth, standout performance in Japan and Australia, where we've partnered with local hyperscalers like AWS Tokyo for low-latency edge computing—DNR at 119%, but accelerating as we navigate data sovereignty regs.

Strategically, this expansion momentum underscores three key initiatives. First, our platform flywheel: 72% of expansions now stem from self-serve discovery within the app, powered by in-product nudges and A/B-tested upsell paths, reducing sales friction and boosting efficiency—our expansion CAC is just 12 months to payback versus 18 for new logos. Second, AI-led retention: Post our ForgeGen 2.0 release, customers using AI modules show 35% higher expansion rates, as it turns our platform into a must-have for hybrid workforces amid persistent remote trends. Third, vertical specialization: We've doubled down on high-ACV verticals—financial services 22% of expansion, healthcare 18%, and manufacturing 14%—with tailored packs, yielding 2x the expansion velocity of horizontal plays.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 expansion to grow 35-40% YoY, supported by our Q4 pipeline of $120 million in committed expansions, assuming stable macro conditions. This positions us to sustain 25%+ overall growth while improving margins.

Shifting to our Rule of 40 performance, which remains a cornerstone metric for SaaS investors benchmarking balanced growth and profitability. For those new to our story, the Rule of 40 simply adds our year-over-year revenue growth percentage to our non-GAAP EBITDA margin percentage. A score above 40 signals we're effectively balancing aggressive expansion with disciplined unit economics—much like how Snowflake and ServiceNow have used it to guide their paths to sustained hypergrowth.

I'm pleased to report that in Q3, we achieved a Rule of 40 score of 48%, up from 42% in Q3 FY2023 and 45% in Q2 of this year. This marks our ninth straight quarter above 40, underscoring the momentum from our platform's AI-driven innovations and our land-and-expand go-to-market strategy.

Revenue growth was 32% YoY—our Q3 revenue hit $178 million, driven primarily by 35% ARR growth to $712 million. This outpaced the SaaS industry average of around 18% as reported by Bessemer Venture Partners' latest Cloud Index. Key contributors included net revenue retention or NRR of 118%, fueled by upsells in our ForgeAI module, our generative AI copilot for workflow orchestration. Customers like a Fortune 500 healthcare provider expanded from 5,000 to 15,000 seats after integrating ForgeAI with their Epic Systems EHR, boosting automation of claims processing by 40%. New logo momentum added 140 net new customers, including three $10M+ mega-logos in financial services—one a top-5 global bank migrating from legacy RPA tools like UiPath. Our focus on mid-market verticals like manufacturing and retail via partner ecosystems with AWS Marketplace contributed 22% of new ARR. North America remains our powerhouse at 68% of revenue, growing 28% YoY amid sticky enterprise adoption. EMEA surged 45% on GDPR-compliant AI features and wins in DACH manufacturing. APAC, now 12% of revenue, grew 62% with our Tokyo data center launch, targeting high-growth sectors like e-commerce in Southeast Asia. Macro headwinds in discretionary IT spend slowed SMB deals, but our 92% gross retention rate held firm, better than the 88% SaaS median per KeyBanc.

EBITDA margin expanded to 16% non-GAAP, up 300 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 450bps YoY. This reflects operational leverage as we scale: Sales & Marketing efficiency improved with CAC payback shrinking to 14 months from 18, thanks to inbound leads from our viral ForgeAI freemium tier—now converting at 28% vs. 19% industry norm. R&D investments yielding returns: We allocated 22% of revenue to R&D, rolling out ForgeAI v2.0 with agentic AI for autonomous decisioning, hyper-focused on no-code workflows. This drove a 25% increase in platform adoption velocity. Operating expenses grew just 22% YoY despite headcount addition of 180 mostly engineering, hitting our 1:3 revenue-to-headcount ratio benchmark.

Our quarterly trend shows steady improvement: Q3 FY2023 had 28% growth and 14% margin for a total of 42; Q2 FY2024 30% growth and 15% margin for 45; now Q3 FY2024 32% growth and 16% margin for 48. We're trending toward a 50%+ score by FY2025, aligning with top-quartile SaaS peers like Datadog amid a market favoring profitable growers. Strategically, we're doubling down on AI moat expansion—60% of Q3 ARR now includes ForgeAI, with multi-modal capabilities positioning us against Adobe Sensei and Salesforce Einstein in enterprise automation. International scaling has APAC ARR set to hit 20% of total by FYE via localized LLMs compliant with data sovereignty regs. Margin runway has free cash flow margin at 12%, up from 8%, with FY2024 guidance implying strong FCF. We're guiding Rule of 40 to 50-55% for FY2025 on 30%+ growth and 20% margins, funded by our solid cash position—no dilution needed. In this environment of elevated interest rates and AI capex scrutiny, our Rule of 40 validates CloudForge as a resilient, high-NRR machine.

Now, turning to churn analysis for Q3, providing a detailed breakdown of the drivers behind customer churn, the trends we're observing, and the multi-faceted strategies we're deploying to mitigate it and drive sustainable retention. In the SaaS landscape, churn is the ultimate litmus test for product-market fit, customer value realization, and our ability to expand within the base. We're particularly proud of our dollar-based NRR of 118% this quarter, up 200 basis points quarter-over-quarter, which reflects strong expansion offsetting modest contraction. However, gross dollar churn ticked up to 7.2% from 6.1% in Q2, primarily in our SMB segment, and logo churn held steady at 4.8%. We've segmented our analysis across cohort vintage, customer tier, geography, and usage patterns, leveraging our proprietary churn prediction models built on XGBoost and powered by Snowflake for real-time data warehousing.

Key reasons for churn: Economic headwinds accounted for about 35% of our voluntary churn. In this high-interest-rate environment—echoing the pressures we've seen across peers like Salesforce and ServiceNow—mid-market customers, particularly those with 10-50 seats, are rationalizing tech stacks. We saw a 15% QoQ increase in budget-constrained cancellations, with ARR impacted cohorts averaging $45K. For instance, a logistics firm in the Midwest cited reallocating funds from CRM expansions to core ops amid softening freight volumes.

Competitive displacement drove another 25% of churn, up from 18% last quarter. Here, we're losing ground in the hyper-competitive CRM space to point solutions like HubSpot for inbound marketing or Pipedrive for lightweight sales automation. Notably, 40% of these losses were in our entry-level Growth tier, where customers perceive us as overkill compared to nimbler alternatives. We've also noted upticks from vertical-specific challengers, such as Toast in hospitality or Mindbody in fitness, poaching via deeper industry workflows.

Product and onboarding friction contributed 20%, centered on time-to-value delays. Our NPS dipped to 52 from 58, with qualitative feedback highlighting integration hurdles—e.g., API latency with legacy ERP systems like NetSuite or QuickBooks. In enterprise deals, 12% of churn tied to unmet SLAs on data migration during onboarding, averaging 45 days to first value versus our 30-day target.

Regionally, North America, 65% of our ARR, churn was stable at 6.5%, buoyed by sticky enterprise logos renewing at +25% expansion. EMEA saw elevated gross churn at 9.1%—driven by GDPR compliance costs and economic slowdowns in Germany and the UK—mirroring trends at companies like UiPath. APAC, now 12% of ARR, experienced 8.4% churn despite 25% YoY bookings growth, largely from local incumbents like Kingdee in China outpacing us on localization. LatAm held at 7.8%, with currency volatility exacerbating dollar-denominated pricing. Involuntary churn—non-payments and expired cards—rose to 2.1% due to payment gateway glitches post-Stripe API updates, but that's noise we'll address imminently.

For mitigation strategies, we're executing a three-pillar playbook: proactive customer health, product-led retention, and go-to-market evolution. Our CSMs have reduced at-risk accounts by 28% YoQ via red-flag interventions.

Pillar one: Customer Success 2.0. We've scaled our CSM-to-ARR ratio to 1:12M from 1:15M, assigning dedicated strategics to top-200 logos. Our ML-powered health scoring model—now at 92% churn prediction accuracy, up from 87%—flags risks 90 days out using 47 signals like login velocity, feature adoption such as our AI Sales Copilot, and expansion intent. Proactive plays include 1:1 QBRs with success plans tied to OKRs, yielding a 65% save rate on predicted churn. We've also launched a Renewal Command Center in Zendesk, automating 70% of renewal workflows with nudge campaigns via Intercom.

Pillar two: Product innovations for stickiness. Q4 sees GA of ForgeAI Insights, our generative AI layer akin to Salesforce Einstein, predicting deal close rates with 85% accuracy and auto-generating personalized outreach—already boosting pilot retention by 22%. Integration velocity is up 40% with native connectors to Microsoft Teams, Slack, and Google Workspace, reducing setup time by 60%. For SMBs, we're piloting usage-based pricing on our Pro tier, mirroring Zuora's flex models, which early data shows cuts churn by 15% via pay-as-you-grow alignment. Enterprise-wise, zero-ETL data sync with Databricks addresses onboarding pain, targeting a 25-day TVT.

Pillar three: Strategic GTM shifts. Pricing rationalization includes a new Essentials tier at $49/user/month, capturing HubSpot defectors and aiming for 10K logos by year-end. Expansion motions are firing on all cylinders: upsell conversion hit 32% via in-app prompts for add-ons like Revenue Intelligence, driving 8.2% net expansion. Regionally, EMEA gets localized GDPR toolkits and Berlin-based support pods; APAC features Mandarin CSM hires and partnerships with Tencent Cloud. We've also stood up a customer advisory board with 15 CIOs, informing roadmaps and unlocking 12 reference deals.

Quantitatively, these efforts are bearing fruit: at-risk ARR dropped 18% QoQ to $14M, and our 0-12 month cohort NRR stabilized at 105%. Looking forward, we guide Q4 gross churn to 6.5-7.0%, trending to sub-6% by year-end as AI features land and macro eases. Long-term, our North Star is 120%+ NRR, fueled by land-and-expand in a $200B TAM expanding at 15% CAGR per Gartner. While churn reflects near-term pressures akin to the 2022 SaaS reset, our data-driven countermeasures position CloudForge for category leadership.

Next, on our liquidity position and cash runway, which remain a cornerstone of our financial strength as we navigate a dynamic SaaS landscape. As of the end of Q3, our cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments stood at $347 million, up 24% from $280 million at the end of Q2 and 41% year-over-year. This robust balance sheet reflects not only our disciplined capital allocation but also the accelerating momentum in our core CRM and analytics platform, which now powers over 12,000 enterprise customers globally.

In Q3, we generated $28 million in operating cash flow, a $15 million improvement sequentially, driven by our record quarterly revenue—up 32% year-over-year—and expanding gross margins of 82%, now firmly in line with top-tier peers like Salesforce and ServiceNow. Our free cash flow turned positive at $12 million for the quarter, marking the second consecutive quarter of FCF positivity after years of strategic investments in R&D and go-to-market scaling. This is ahead of our initial guidance for FCF breakeven by year-end, underscoring the leverage in our SaaS model as NRR hit 118%—fueled by upsells in our AI-powered predictive analytics module, which saw 45% adoption among our top 500 customers.

Our cash burn has meaningfully improved. Trailing twelve-month net cash used in operations narrowed to just $18 million, down from $52 million a year ago, thanks to several key levers. First, sales and marketing efficiency: Our dollar-based net expansion rate held steady at 125%, allowing us to reduce CAC payback to under 14 months, even as we ramped enterprise deals in competitive verticals like financial services and healthcare. Second, operating expense discipline—opex as a percentage of revenue dropped to 68% from 75% last year—without compromising innovation. We're prioritizing high-ROI initiatives, such as our GenAI integrations akin to Adobe's Firefly or HubSpot's Breeze, which are already contributing 15% to new ARR bookings.

Regionally, this cash generation is broad-based. North America remains our cash cow, accounting for 65% of Q3 cash inflows with ARR growth of 35% YoY, bolstered by multi-year renewals from Fortune 500 names. EMEA delivered a standout 48% YoY revenue surge—our fastest-growing region—thanks to GDPR-compliant expansions and wins with European telcos, generating $9 million in incremental cash flow. APAC, while still ramping at 28% YoY, is cash flow neutral as we invest in localization for markets like Japan and India, where we've seen 60% quarter-over-quarter growth in SMB segments via our low-touch self-serve channel.

Looking ahead, our expected cash runway exceeds 42 months at current burn rates, assuming moderate revenue growth in line with our FY24 guide of strong ARR growth. Even in a downside scenario with macroeconomic headwinds—like persistent high interest rates squeezing venture funding for our smaller competitors—we maintain a conservative 30-month runway after factoring in a 10% revenue deceleration and flat headcount. This visibility gives us tremendous flexibility.

Strategically, we're deploying this liquidity across three pillars: $50 million earmarked for FY25 R&D, focusing on agentic AI workflows that embed seamlessly into tools like Microsoft Teams and Slack—mirroring Zoom's pivot to AI companions amid hybrid work persistence; $100-150 million for tuck-in M&A in vertical SaaS, such as compliance add-ons for fintech, similar to how monday.com has layered on capabilities post-IPO; and shareholder returns and resilience, with no debt on the balance sheet, and we're exploring a modest share repurchase if valuations remain depressed—our EV/ARR multiple of 7.2x is a 40% discount to the median SaaS peer at 12x, per Bessemer Cloud Index data.

In summary, our $347 million war chest positions CloudForge not just to weather industry cycles—like the ongoing ARR contraction at some high-burn players—but to accelerate market share gains. We have no near-term funding needs and are committed to driving toward sustained 20%+ FCF margins as we scale.

Finally, turning to our outlook for Q4 FY24. Before I dive into the specifics, let me reiterate that our business remains fundamentally strong amid a dynamic macro environment. We've seen continued resilience in enterprise spending on mission-critical SaaS workloads, particularly around AI-infused analytics and cloud-native data platforms—trends we're capitalizing on with our ForgeAI platform. Our dollar-based net retention—or NRR—held steady at 118% in Q3, driven by 25% expansion revenue from existing customers upsell into our new AI Query Engine and Multi-Cloud Federation modules. Churn remains best-in-class at under 4% gross dollar churn for enterprise cohorts, well below industry averages reported by peers like Snowflake and Datadog.

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, we are guiding to ending ARR of $765 million to $775 million. This represents sequential growth of 7% to 9% from our Q3 ending ARR of $712 million, and year-over-year growth of 30% to 32%. To put this in context, this guidance embeds approximately $45 million to $55 million in new Annual Contract Value—or ACV—bookings, with a healthy mix of 60% coming from net new logos and 40% from expansions and renewals.

Key drivers: New logo momentum, 40-45% of Q4 bookings—we're expecting strong performance from our enterprise sales motion, targeting Fortune 1000 accounts in financial services and healthcare. In Q3, we landed eight deals over $5 million ACV, including a landmark win with a top-5 global bank migrating from legacy BI tools to our fully managed, AI-accelerated platform. For Q4, we anticipate 12-15 such large deals, fueled by our Freemium-to-Enterprise funnel, where we've seen trial-to-paid conversion rates climb to 28%—up 300 basis points quarter-over-quarter—thanks to integrations with Snowflake's marketplace and AWS Bedrock for seamless GenAI embeddings.

Expansion and land-and-expand, 30-35% of bookings: Our NRR guidance for Q4 is 116% to 120%, reflecting continued upsell into high-velocity add-ons. Customers are expanding seats by an average of 22% upon adopting our Predictive Analytics Suite, which leverages LLMs for anomaly detection and forecasting. We've also seen multi-year renewals at 105%+ net pricing, countering any pricing pressure in SMB segments.

Retention and churn outlook remains low single digits: Gross revenue churn guidance at 3.5% to 4.5%, with multi-year contracts now comprising 75% of our ARR base—up from 68% a year ago. This durability gives us conviction even as we navigate potential elongation in sales cycles for deals under $1 million ACV.

Regional breakdown and tailwinds: North America, 65% of ARR, core growth at 28% YoY, anchored by hyperscaler partnerships. US Federal bookings accelerated via our FedRAMP High authorization, expected to contribute meaningfully. EMEA, 20% of ARR, fastest-growing at 45% YoY, driven by GDPR-compliant AI features and wins with DAX 40 firms. APAC, 10% of ARR, 25% YoY growth guidance, with investments in Tokyo and Sydney data centers paying off, targeting 20% ACV from Japan and ANZ, bolstered by native support for Alibaba Cloud and Tencent integrations. Rest of World steady at 20% YoY.

This guidance assumes no material deterioration in the macro backdrop, including sustained interest rates and delayed AI CapEx from cautious CISOs. On the opportunity side, our Q4 launch of ForgeAI Copilot—an agentic AI coprocessor for natural language querying—positions us to capture share in the BI/Analytics TAM, akin to how dbt and Hex are reshaping modern data stacks. We've already secured beta commitments from 50+ customers representing $100 million potential ARR expansion over the next 12 months.

We're also guiding Q4 total revenue to $185 million to $190 million, with non-GAAP operating margins expanding to 28% to 30%, reflecting 75%+ gross margins and disciplined OpEx at 52% of revenue. RPO remains a bright spot, with current remaining performance obligations growing 35% YoY.

In summary, this Q4 ARR guide keeps us firmly on track for $800 million+ exiting FY24, with multi-year ARR growth north of 30%. We're executing at scale in a market where AI is redefining SaaS economics, and our focus on sticky, high-NRR workflows gives us durable moats.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong for a technology update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Emily Santos will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Emily Santos:
Thank you, Lisa. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Insights. This new feature significantly improves workflow optimization and predictive analytics. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy of delivering AI-native tools for enterprise teams.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Jordan Lee:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Jordan. ForgeAI has been a game-changer for our growth, contributing over 25% of new ARR in Q3 through upsells and new logos. We're seeing attach rates of around 45% on existing customers, particularly in enterprise where it drives 20%+ ACV uplift. This is well ahead of our initial expectations, where we modeled 30% attach—early traction from integrations and the freemium model has accelerated adoption, positioning it as core to our land-and-expand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

David Harper:
Great question, Emily. International expansion remains a top priority, with APAC as a key focus given its growth potential. We're investing in localized data centers in Tokyo and Sydney, Mandarin support, and partnerships with Alibaba Cloud and Tencent to reduce latency and ensure compliance. Key target markets include Japan for enterprise manufacturing, Australia for financial services, and Southeast Asia e-commerce verticals. We expect APAC to reach 15% of ARR by FY25, building on 35% QoQ new logo growth and 125% NRR in early cohorts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Baker with Barclays.

Tom Baker:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Tom. As detailed earlier, we're managing churn proactively through our three-pillar approach—enhanced customer success with ML prediction at 92% accuracy, product innovations like ForgeAI Insights reducing time-to-value, and GTM shifts including new pricing tiers. Gross dollar churn was 7.2% this quarter, but NRR trended up to 118%, with expansions more than offsetting. Strategies include scaling CSMs, automating renewals, and vertical-specific packs, guiding Q4 churn lower to 6.5-7.0% while targeting 120%+ NRR long-term.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Harper for closing remarks.

David Harper:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Next quarter ARR guidance: Provide ARR guidance for the next quarter.
Churn analysis: Discuss reasons for customer churn and mitigation strategies.
